transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because of something happening at work. For months I’ve been noticing patterns in the project files—small changes in the translation memory and timestamps. It looks like certain subcontractors, and one colleague, are setting things up so it seems like my quality control failed.

IT says the audit trail is clean, but… I don’t think that means much. The record can be arranged. I know it’s being made to put the blame on me.
Do you think it's possible that there's another explanation for the changes you've noticed in the project files?

I’ve considered that, yes. But it’s the same pattern over and over—tiny changes in the translation memory, timestamps lining up strangely, always involving the same subcontractors and one colleague. IT says the audit trail is clean, but I don’t really trust that. It feels arranged so it lands on me.
How long have you been noticing these patterns in the project files?
About eleven months, I think. It started not long after I was put in charge of the new localization project.
Do you think these changes in the project files are somehow related to you personally, beyond just affecting your work?
Yes. I mean… it’s not just random file errors. It feels directed at me. The changes make it look like I missed things in quality control, like they’re trying to put the blame on me specifically.
Do you believe that other things in your life, outside of work, are also connected to this plot against you?

No… not really outside of work. I still do my usual things—translate, handle the team workflow, pay bills, family routines. It’s mostly when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers are involved, that things start feeling… connected.
Do you ever have times when you don't think someone is plotting against you at work?

When I’m not dealing with those project files, I can put it aside a bit. But once I see the same subcontractors or that colleague involved, or the timestamps and translation memory changes show up again… no, then I don’t really think it’s just nothing. Even if IT says the audit trail is clean, it looks arranged to make my quality control look bad.
Do you think that things you see or hear on the news, or things that strangers say to you, are somehow related to what's going on at work with the project files?

No… I don’t think it’s the news or strangers. It’s really the project files. The same subcontractors, and one colleague, keep showing up around these little changes in the translation memory and timestamps. Even when IT says it’s clean, it looks arranged to put the blame on my quality control.
Do you ever have moments, even if briefly, when you completely doubt that someone is plotting against you at work?

Completely doubt it? Not really. I might step away from it for a while, but when I look back at the files, the same pattern is there—the subcontractors, that one colleague, the translation memory, the timestamps. Even if IT says it’s clean, it feels arranged to make it look like my quality control failed.
Do you think the people involved in this plot against you are working together in an organized way?

Yes… I think so. Not some huge operation, but coordinated enough. It’s the same subcontractors and that one colleague, and the changes are too consistent—the translation memory, the timestamps. It looks arranged so the quality control failure lands on me.
Do you think the plot against you at work is part of a larger plan that affects other areas of your life or other people?

No… I don’t think it’s bigger than work. It’s about the project files. For months it’s been the same pattern—certain subcontractors and one colleague making small changes to the translation memory and timestamps, so it looks like my quality control failed. IT says the audit trail is clean, but… I know the record’s been arranged to put it on me.
Do you think the people involved in this plot against you have a specific goal in mind for what they want to achieve by blaming you for the quality control failures?

Yes. I think the goal is to make it look like I missed things—like my quality control failed. The little changes in the translation memory and timestamps… it all points that way. Even if IT says the audit trail is clean, it feels like the record’s been set up so the blame lands on me.
Do you think the plot against you at work is something that you've figured out completely, or are there still parts of it that you're trying to understand?

I don’t think I’ve figured out all of it. I’ve figured out the pattern, though… the same subcontractors, that one colleague, small changes in the translation memory and timestamps. Enough to know the record’s being arranged so the quality control blame falls on me. But how they’re keeping it looking clean to IT… I’m still trying to understand that.
Do you think the plot against you at work is something that is happening only to you, or could it potentially happen to someone else in your position?

I think it’s mostly aimed at me… because it’s my quality control they’re making look bad. But I suppose if someone else were in my position, handling the same project files, they could do the same kind of thing to them too. The pattern is in the translation memory and the timestamps… it’s not random.
Are there any times when you completely forget about the plot against you at work?

Not completely, no. I mean, I can be doing other things and not talk about it, but it’s still… there. For months it’s been the same pattern in the files—those small changes in the translation memory and timestamps, the same people around it—so it’s hard to just forget.
Have you ever had a time when you believed the plot against you at work was not happening or was less serious than you think it is now?

Maybe at the beginning I wondered if I was reading too much into it. But after months of seeing the same pattern in the project files… the same subcontractors, the same colleague, those little changes to the translation memory and timestamps… no, I don’t really think it’s less serious now. Even if IT says the audit trail is clean, it feels arranged so the blame lands on me.
If IT were to show you proof that the changes in the project files were due to a technical error, would you still believe that someone is plotting against you?

If they showed me something like that, I’d look at it, but… I don’t think it would settle it for me. IT already says the audit trail is clean, and that’s part of what bothers me. The changes and timestamps still seem arranged so the blame comes back on my quality control.
Would seeing proof from IT that the changes were accidental change your mind about someone plotting against you?

Probably not completely. I’d look at what IT showed me, but the same pattern has been there for months—those tiny changes in the translation memory and timestamps, the same people around it. Even if they call it accidental, it still feels like the record is being set up so the blame lands on my quality control.
Do you think you could ever be completely wrong about someone plotting against you at work?

Completely wrong? I… I don’t really see how. I’ve watched the same pattern in the files for months—the translation memory, the timestamps, the same people connected to it. IT can say the audit trail is clean, but to me it still looks arranged so the blame comes back on my quality control.
How certain are you that someone is plotting against you at work?

I’m… very certain. I know that may sound strong, but I’ve been seeing the same pattern for months—the translation memory, the timestamps, certain subcontractors, one colleague. It looks arranged so my quality control takes the blame, even if IT says the audit trail is clean.
